planning_notes: Button polarity: digital inputs on D2/D3/D4 use pullups and active_high=false, so model 'pressed' corresponds to logic true when the pin reads LOW (do not double-invert).

Control period (10 ms) is scheduling granularity; the 2-second minimum state maintenance/verification delay must be implemented in the SysML model using elapsed_ms deltas and model-level timing, not in these port requests.

RGB LED is common cathode; the pwm_output channels are set so that 0 means off at startup (all channels initial=0). Model must drive exactly one of R/G/B to represent the required color states: btn1->red, btn2->green, btn3->blue.
Startup requirement: servo1 and servo2 at 0 degrees and RGB LED off are satisfied by servo_angle initial=0 and RGB PWM initial=0; subsequent 90-degree/color states are handled in SysML.
No serial reporting is required by the prose; serial_channels is intentionally empty.

interfaces.name: io_0
interfaces.meaning: btn1: set servo1=90deg and RGB to red (hold at least 2s in model)

interfaces.name: io_1
interfaces.meaning: btn2: set servo2=90deg and RGB to green (hold at least 2s in model)

interfaces.name: io_2
interfaces.meaning: btn3: reset both servos to 0deg and RGB to blue (hold at least 2s in model)

**Task**:
You are tasked with programming an Arduino (uno) to control two servos (servo1, servo2) and an RGB LED (rgb1) using three push buttons (btn1, btn2, btn3). The RGB LED will display different colors based on the state of the servos, and the push buttons will control the movement of the servos and the color of the RGB LED.

**Detail Rules**:
Initialization: Upon powering on or resetting, both servos (servo1, servo2) should be at their 0-degree position, and the RGB LED (rgb1) should be off.
Button Interaction:
1. The first button (btn1) will rotate servo1 (servo1) to 90 degrees and set the RGB LED (rgb1) to red.
2. The second button (btn2) will rotate servo2 (servo2) to 90 degrees and set the RGB LED (rgb1) to green.
3. The third button (btn3) will reset both servos (servo1, servo2) to their 0-degree position and set the RGB LED (rgb1) to blue.
Each state (servo position and LED color) should be maintained for at least 2 seconds to allow for verification.
